does: Brushes a rolled round of atta dough with ghee, dusts it with a little flour, and folds it over on itself into a half-moon and then a triangle, so that the dough is stacked in thin layers with ghee between them. The folded piece is then rolled out again, lightly.
how: Brush the whole rolled round with soft ghee and dust it with a little dry flour.
Fold the round in half to a half-moon, brush the top with ghee again and dust it lightly.
Fold the half-moon in half once more, into a triangle with its layers stacked inside.
Press the edges gently so that the layers stay together, and roll the triangle out lightly with even strokes.

cues.text: The cut edge of the folded triangle shows thin stripes of dough and ghee.
The triangle rolls out smoothly and the layers do not slide apart.

mistakes.mistake: Rolling hard after folding, so that the ghee is pressed out and the layers fuse into one.
mistakes.fix: Roll lightly and evenly, and stop as soon as the triangle is the size of the plate.

mistakes.mistake: Leaving the dough dry between the folds, so that the finished bread is tough and not flaky.
mistakes.fix: Brush every fold with ghee, right to the edges.

comes_after.why: The folds start from a round of dough that is rolled even, so a cook has to be able to roll one first.

variant_of.differs: The dough is a soft atta dough that is not rested between folds, the fat is ghee brushed on by hand, and it is folded once or twice into a half-moon or triangle and rolled out again lightly. It is not a pastry that is turned and rolled many times.
